To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Mg II absorbers at intermediate redshift are multiphase, with ionization conditions ranging from low (e.g., C III/C IV < 1) to high (e.g., N V/C IV < 0.2).
Mg II absorbers have multiphase gas with a wide range of physical conditions, and the ionization conditions are not correlated with the strength of the absorption systems.

the absorption-selected Mg II absorbers at z∼ 1 have (1) a wide range of column densities and ionization conditions, (2) low-ionization gas that is often associated with the galaxy, (3) high-ionization gas that may be associated with the galaxy but is more likely to be associated with the IGM, and (4) the low- and high-ionization gas are not always co-located in velocity space.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: (1) the relationship between Mg II and Fe II absorption; (2) the ionization properties of the Mg II-selected absorbers; (3) the relationship between the Mg II-selected absorption and galaxy properties; (4) the relationship between metal-line absorption and the Lyman-alpha forest at the absorbers' redshifts; and (5) the relationship between Lyman-alpha absorption and the metal-line absorption at the absorbers’ redshifts.

the properties of galaxies at intermediate red-shifts (0.4 < z < 1.4) as traced by Mg II absorption systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Mg II absorption selected galaxies at intermediate redshfits have multiphase, metal-rich gaseous structures that show evidence for a wide range of physical conditions.
the Mg II-selected galaxies are a heterogeneous group of galaxies that have a wide variety of ionization and excitation conditions.

Mg II-selected absorption systems are composed of a multiphase medium, which is characterized by a warm, low-ionization, and high column density phase, and a warm, high-ionization and low column density phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the absorption properties of the galaxies can be understood in terms of two phases, one that is primarily ionized by the ultraviolet radiation of the galaxy and a second phase that is primarily ionizing by the cosmic ultraviolet background.

the absorption systems are comprised of a cool (T ∼ 104 K) phase that has a high covering fraction, a warm (T ∼ (3-6) x 105 K) phase that also has a high covering factor, and a hot (T > 106 K) phase that is less common but has a large ionization parameter.

Mg II absorbers are metal-enriched, have a wide range of gas temperatures, and have ionization conditions ranging from photoionized to collisionally ionized, and in some instances, are likely to be in a multiphase medium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Mg II absorbers at intermediate redshift are not a simple extension of local absorbers.
there is a wide range in ionization conditions in Mg II absorbers at z = 0.4-1.4.
the low-ionization phase is the most abundant, but the high-ionization phase is more highly ionized and more metal-rich than the low-ionization gas.
